answer: The Go server rewrite was decided first. `ADR/008 Go Backend.md` is dated 2025-09-19. The client toolchain move from Deno to Node is in `ADR/009 Client Build Toolchain.md`, dated 2026-03-10.

ADR/008 Go Backend.md:19:Rewrite the server in **Go**. Being just a file store, the whole backend was ported becoming significantly less memory and significantly smaller in size than the Deno build.
ADR/010 Rust Backend.md:21:The server has been, in turn: Node.js (earliest prototypes), then **Deno** for years, then **Go** (2025), and now **Rust** (2026). (The separate move of the *client* build toolchain from Deno to Node is [[ADR/009 Client Build Toolchain|its own decision]].) This is further discussed in [On Tech Stacks](https://no.silverbullet.md/tech-stacks).
ADR/010 Rust Backend.md:41:* **Revert the server to TypeScript (Deno or Node).** Rejected: a JS runtime buys little for a process that just serves files and it is resource heavy.
ADR/009 Client Build Toolchain.md:23:The client build toolchain moved from **Deno to Node.js** (npm + ESBuild, with [vitest](https://vitest.dev/) for tests). It was done gradually and completed in the `to-node` migration.
ADR/009 Client Build Toolchain.md:32:* **More moving parts.** Deno bundled fmt/lint/test out of the box. On Node these are assembled from separate packages (biome, vitest), a slightly larger dependency surface.
CHANGELOG.md:325:* **Technical: Deno → Node.js migration**: The TypeScript/client codebase has been migrated from Deno to Node.js, now using vitest for tests.
